rounds.text: Chartered Logistics faces a fundamental crisis of profitability, evidenced by a compounded profit growth of -222% over the trailing twelve months [E14] and a negative return on equity of -5.5% [E12]. The company’s operational efficiency is in a long-term state of decay, with operating margins trending downward over the last four years [E23] and currently sitting at a meager 1% [E21]. This poor performance is compounded by an alarming valuation disconnect, where the EV/EBITDA ratio of 32.48x significantly exceeds the sector benchmark of 10.19x [E10]. Furthermore, the erosion of confidence is reflected in the promoter group, who have reduced their stake by 13.60 percentage points since December 2023 [E32]. The company also struggles with a low interest coverage ratio [E39] and relies on other income of Rs 2.47 Cr to bolster its earnings profile [E42]. Conceded: the company maintains comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 2.24x [E29] and generated positive free cash flow of Rs 4.36 Cr in March 2026 [E27].

While the bear highlights negative profit growth [E14] and ROE [E12], it ignores the critical reality that the company is currently generating significant cash, with Rs 6.94 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 4.36 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E26, E27]. The focus on a high EV/EBITDA ratio [E10] overlooks that the company is priced at a modest 1.41x price-to-book ratio [E1], which is nearly in line with the sector benchmark [E6]. Conceded: promoter holding has decreased [E32, E43] and operating margins have trended downward [E23]. However, the bear fails to acknowledge the recent institutional interest, as domestic institutions have initiated a position [E34] and the overall money flow is currently positive [E35]. Furthermore, the company maintains a strong liquidity position with a current ratio of 2.24x [E29], providing the necessary stability to navigate the current cyclical earnings phase [E38]. Finally, the bear’s reliance on trailing metrics ignores the most recent evidence of accelerating earnings growth and quarter-over-quarter profit improvements [E45, E46].
